profile.reading: The building recorded here carries only the initials MDC, tagged directly onto the structure at 11455 Cedar Oak Drive in the Las Palmas neighborhood on El Paso's east side, an ordinary residential and light commercial part of the city rather than a known data center corridor. Three letter acronyms of this kind are too generic to identify a specific company without an independent record, and MDC could plausibly stand for many different things, a business name, a medical or municipal facility, or a telecommunications equipment designation, with nothing in the available mapping data or public business listings to disambiguate it. No operator website, news coverage, or business registration naming MDC as a data center company at this El Paso address could be located and independently confirmed. El Paso does host real telecommunications and IT infrastructure serving the broader West Texas and Ciudad Juarez border region, so a small facility of some kind at this address is plausible in principle, but the acronym alone is not sufficient grounds to describe this as a confirmed, named data center operator.
profile.research_note: Nominatim confirms a building at 11455 Cedar Oak Dr, El Paso TX, in the Las Palmas neighborhood (residential/light commercial east side); OSM building tag is literally "MDC". A guessed mdcelpaso.com does not resolve. El Paso Central Appraisal District quicksearch URL guess returned 404. No company or registry record identified. Acronym too generic and no lead found; genuinely unresolved.

reading.body:
A building tagged MDC at 11455 Cedar Oak Drive in El Paso cannot be confirmed as a data center because its operator remains unidentified and the acronym is too generic to verify without independent documentation.

El Paso does operate real telecommunications infrastructure serving West Texas and the Ciudad Juarez border region, making a small facility plausible at this location. The building sits in a residential and light commercial neighborhood on the city's east side rather than in any known data center corridor. No operator website, news coverage, business registration, or public records could identify what MDC stands for or who operates it. The acronym could refer to a business name, medical facility, municipal office, or telecommunications equipment designation.

No power consumption, rack capacity, or cooling specifications have been published for this facility. Without these specifications, its computational capacity and relevance to grid load or AI scaling cannot be assessed. The unresolved status means MDC does not figure in any current count of Texas's available compute infrastructure or published capacity.
